---
title: "Check disclosure before sharing results"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(easyNIS)
library(dplyr)
library(srvyr)
library(gtsummary)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

The examples use invented data.

## Count the discharges and hospitals behind each cell

```{r support}
nis <- nis_open(nis_example(years = 2019:2020)) |>
  nis_flag_dx(heart_failure = "I50")
counts <- nis_cell_counts(nis, by = c(YEAR, heart_failure))
counts
```

The HCUP Data Use Agreement prohibits publishing cells based on 1 through
10 sampled discharges and prohibits publishing identifying information.
easyNIS also masks statistics supported by fewer than two hospitals.
Check support for the records contributing to each statistic.
[HCUP Data Use Agreement](https://hcup-us.ahrq.gov/team/NationwideDUA.jsp)

## Mask a summary and check what can be recovered

```{r complementary}
groups <- nis |>
  mutate(age_group = if_else(AGE >= 87, "87 and older", "under 87"))
cells <- nis_cell_counts(groups, by = c(YEAR, age_group))
cells |>
  nis_suppress(count_col = n, hospital_col = hospitals,
               by = YEAR, secondary = TRUE)
```

If the year total is public, a reader can subtract the published age group
to recover the masked group. Complementary suppression hides another
value to prevent that deduction. The data-frame helper can mask the
smallest remaining positive cell when a group has one primary mask. Keep
totals out of that input and decide which totals can be released. The
helper also masks zeros as a conservative default.

## Mask a survey table

```{r table}
design <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, RACE, heart_failure))
tbl_svysummary(design, by = heart_failure, include = c(AGE, RACE)) |>
  nis_suppress() |>
  as_gt()
```

The helper checks the non-missing complement of a displayed two-level
indicator and masks related overall statistics when a group is masked.
If exactly one level of a categorical variable is masked in a column,
the helper also masks the smallest remaining positive level in that column.
Check whether percentages, totals, or other outputs reveal a masked cell
before release.

## Export a three-group table to CSV

```{r export-table}
bands <- nis |>
  mutate(age_group = case_when(
    AGE >= 90 ~ "90 and older",
    AGE >= 65 ~ "65 to 89",
    AGE >= 18 ~ "18 to 64"
  ))
age_design <- nis_design(bands, cohort = AGE >= 18, keep = c(age_group, LOS))
masked <- tbl_svysummary(age_design, by = age_group, include = LOS) |>
  nis_suppress()
csv <- tibble::as_tibble(masked) |>
  mutate(across(-1L, ~ sub("\u2264", "<=", .x, fixed = TRUE)))
file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(csv, file, row.names = FALSE)
read.csv(file, check.names = FALSE)
```

Suppression masks the oldest group's denominator and statistics.
`as_tibble()` carries the masked heading into the CSV. The export uses
the ASCII marker `<=` for compatibility with non-UTF-8 locales. Review
the CSV alongside the other outputs you plan to share.

## Scan the finished publication folder

```{r publication-scan}
publication <- tempfile("publication-")
dir.create(publication)
write.csv(counts, file.path(publication, "draft-counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
nis_scan_outputs(publication)
```

Run the scan on the folder you plan to publish. It reports file paths,
locations, and finding types for recognized identifiers and small counts.
Use `error = TRUE` to stop on findings. Review images, charts, hospital
support, and counts that readers could infer from related outputs.
See [`nis_scan_outputs()`](../reference/nis_scan_outputs.html) for the
supported formats and patterns.
